pictures.scene: Caravaggio, Supper at Emmaus — a beardless young Christ in a scarlet tunic and white mantle seated in the middle of a laid table with His eyes lowered and one hand raised over the bread, His head throwing a great shadow on the brown wall behind Him, a bald bearded old man leaning in at His left with both hands lifted, another man at the far edge with his arm flung out, and the white cloth before them covered with a roast fowl on a painted dish, loaves, a basket of grapes, pomegranates and pears and a glass of wine, six days before the passover, jesus came to bethany, the hometown of lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead, so they hosted a dinner for jesus there, …
pictures.name: pd_caravaggio_supper_at_emmaus

pictures.scene: Dieric Bouts, Christ in the House of Simon — a woman in a green gown and a deep blue and red mantle bowed right down to the tiled floor with her long fair hair spread over the bare feet of Christ, wiping them with it while her lidded white ointment jar stands open beside her on the tiles, Christ seated behind the laid table in a dark blue robe with His hand raised in blessing and His eyes lowered toward her, a bearded host in a jewelled blue cap and an olive gown at His shoulder, and on the white cloth between them loaves, a green glass and a fish on a pewter dish, then mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair, and the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume, …
pictures.name: pd_bouts_anointing

pictures.scene: Quentin Metsys, The Moneylender and His Wife — a man in a wide black fur-edged cap and a brown gown weighing coins on a small pair of scales, his eyes fixed down on the pan and the loose gold and silver lying on the counter in front of him, his wife beside him in a scarlet gown and a white headdress turning the leaves of an illuminated book but with her eyes slid sideways to the money, a convex mirror on the counter showing a window with a cross bar in it, and a shelf of pewter, an apple, papers and books along the wall above, judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief, as keeper of the money bag, he used to take from what was put into it, …
pictures.name: pd_metsys_the_moneylender_and_his_wife

pictures.scene: Master of Alkmaar, The Seven Works of Mercy, Feeding the Hungry — a housewife in a white headdress and a long white apron standing in her doorway with a basket of round loaves held out before her, handing bread into the hands of a crowd of the poor gathered in the street, a woman in green with a child at her back taking a loaf, an old man in a red cloak, a mother with a baby reaching up, a legless beggar on the cobbles below with his crutches beside him, a small brown dog sitting by the house wall, and Christ standing quietly in the middle of the press watching, the poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have me, …
pictures.name: pd_alkmaar_barmhartigheid

pictures.scene: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, The Census at Bethlehem — a snowbound village under a cold green-grey winter sky with a bare tree spreading right across it and a small red sun setting behind the branches, a great press of country people in hoods and heavy coats crowded round the window of an inn where the registrars sit writing at a table, more of them trudging in across the frozen river where children are skating and sliding, a loaded cart and a cartwheel in the snow at the front, men sawing timber and chickens scratching in the trodden white, meanwhile a large crowd of jews learned that jesus was there, and they came not only because of him, but also to see lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead, …
pictures.name: pd_bruegel_volkstelling

pictures.scene: Frederic Edwin Church, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the whole city lying along the far ridge behind its long tawny wall, its domes and flat roofs and the great blue-tiled dome of the temple platform catching a hazy gold light, with a towering bank of cloud rising over it into a warm yellow sky, the Kidron valley below falling away in dark olive terraces scattered with olive trees, and in the foreground a stony white track coming up over the hill where two laden camels and three travellers stand looking across at the city, the next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that jesus was coming to jerusalem, …
pictures.name: pd_church_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

pictures.scene: Pieter Aertsen, The Entry into Jerusalem — Christ in a grey tunic and a great crimson mantle riding down the hill road on a donkey covered with a yellow patterned cloth, two fingers lifted in blessing, bearded disciples pressing close at the donkey's head, and in front of Him men stooping to spread their red and gold cloaks out flat across the stones of the road, a crowd coming over the ridge behind with branches and children, and thin windblown trees against a pale sky at the top, they took palm branches and went out to meet him, shouting, hosanna, blessed is he who comes in the name of the lord, blessed is the king of israel, …
pictures.name: pd_aertsen_entry_jerusalem

pictures.scene: Adam Elsheimer, The Flight into Egypt — a night sky thick with painted stars running right across the top of the picture, a full moon low on the right throwing a long silver track down a still water, great black masses of oak and willow standing against the starlight, and at the foot of them Joseph in a red jacket walking barefoot beside the donkey with a lighted torch in his hand, leading Mary in a blue-grey veil with the Child held close against her shoulder, see, your king is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey, …
pictures.name: pd_elsheimer_the_flight_into_egypt

pictures.scene: Emanuel de Witte, Interior of the Oude Kerk in Amsterdam during a Sermon — a tall whitewashed gothic church of pale arches, round piers and traceried windows, a preacher in black leaning out of the high wooden pulpit with his hand put out as he speaks, hearers in wide black hats listening in the panelled pews below, a woman in a hood holding a little book with a small boy in yellow beside her, a brown and white dog sitting in a patch of sunlight on the floor stones, and gold chandeliers and a carved organ case hanging in the aisle beyond, meanwhile, many people continued to testify that they had been with jesus when he called lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead, …
pictures.name: pd_de_witte_interior_of_the_oude_kerk_amsterdam_during_a_sermon

pictures.scene: Jan Gossaert, The Adoration of the Kings, the retinue of Balthasar — foreign lords standing close together against a rough brick and stone wall, the dark-skinned king in front in a high jewelled crown and a gold brocade gown with a pale blue mantle over his shoulder, setting down a tall gothic goldsmith's vessel at the edge of the picture, a fair young attendant beside him in a red cap and a green and blue embroidered tabard, another in a great blue turban and a fur-collared coat, and a third face looking out between them, with a white and blue banner and a green damask hanging above, now there were some greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast, …
pictures.name: pd_gossaert_the_kings_retinue

pictures.scene: Raphael, Saint Paul Preaching at Athens — a bearded apostle standing barefoot on a stone step in a green tunic and a great salmon-red mantle, seen from behind with both hands thrown up above his head as he speaks, Greeks seated and crouching on the pavement all round him listening, one leaning his chin on his fist, a curly-headed youth staring straight out, an old man in a cap looking up from the shadow at the left, and behind them the grey piers, arches and cornices of the city, they came to philip, who was from bethsaida in galilee, and requested of him, sir, we want to see jesus, …
pictures.name: pd_raphael_saint_paul_preaching_at_athens

pictures.scene: Jean-Francois Millet, The Sower — a peasant in a battered hat, a red-brown jacket and blue trousers striding down the turned earth of a hillside at dusk, his seed bag slung across his body and gripped in his left hand, his right arm swung wide and open in the act of casting the grain, his boots bound round with rags and sinking into the clods, a grey evening sky behind him and a last streak of warm light on a far ridge, truly, truly, i tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed, but if it dies, it bears much fruit, …
pictures.name: pd_millet_the_sower

pictures.scene: Gerrit Dou, Old Woman Reading a Lectionary — a very old woman in a fur cap and a pleated linen headband, wrapped in a heavy blue-grey gown with a wide fur collar fastened by a gold clasp, holding a great printed book up in both wrinkled hands and bending her face right down over it, the light falling full on her lined cheek and on the open leaves with their columns of black letter and a small woodcut set into the page, the room behind her nothing but quiet olive-brown shadow, if anyone serves me, he must follow me, and where i am, my servant will be as well, …
pictures.name: pd_dou_overdenking

pictures.scene: El Greco, The Agony in the Garden — Christ kneeling alone on the bare ground in a rose-pink robe over a deep crimson tunic, His blue mantle fallen in folds all round His knees, both hands opened wide and held out from His sides and His face lifted and turned up to the sky, a great tawny rock rising close behind Him with thin dry scrub growing out of its clefts, and pale rolling cloud pressing in at either edge of the picture, now my soul is troubled, and what shall i say, father, save me from this hour, no, it is for this purpose that i have come to this hour, …
pictures.name: pd_el_greco_the_agony_in_the_garden

pictures.scene: John Martin, Belshazzar's Feast — a vast torchlit Babylonian banquet hall at night, a great roll of black smoke and storm cloud crossing the sky above with a tall lit ziggurat tower standing up into it, tiered tan walls, columns and carved friezes dropping away in long perspective, files of tiny torchbearers climbing the stairs, and at the bottom a long white-clothed table loaded with gold cups, bowls and dishes, a bearded prophet in a black robe standing in the middle of it with his arm flung straight up and out as he speaks, women in white gowns starting back from him with their hands thrown above their heads, guests crowded shoulder to shoulder away into the dark, and dark-robed attendants with staves at the near corner, the crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered, others said that an angel had spoken to him, …
pictures.name: pd_john_martin_belshazzars_feast

pictures.scene: Bartolome Bermejo, Saint Michael Triumphant over the Devil — a young archangel standing full height in burnished gilt plate armour and mail with a crimson silk mantle billowing out behind him across a tooled gold ground, his great orange and red wings spread wide, the sword lifted back over his head in his mailed fist and a glass and gold shield held out in his bare hand, his foot set down on the scaled back of a horned red-eyed demon sprawling among the rocks below, and a donor in a tall black cap and a silver brocade gown kneeling at the left with an open book in his hands, looking up, now judgment is upon this world, now the prince of this world will be cast out, …
pictures.name: pd_bermejo_saint_michael_triumphant_over_the_devil

pictures.scene: Hieronymus Bosch, Christ Carrying the Cross — an all over press of faces packed from edge to edge with no air between them, Christ in the middle of them with His eyes closed and His head fallen sideways under the crown of thorns, the long pale beam of the cross laid across His shoulder and running out of the top corner, and crowding in on every side the jeering heads of His escort, a man in a white turban snarling with his teeth bared, a hook nosed face in a black hood with a ring in his ear, a soldier in a blue cap with his eyes starting and his mouth open, a tall blue and gold hat, a red helmet hung with chains at the bottom corner, he said this to indicate the kind of death he was going to die, …
pictures.name: pd_bosch_christ_carrying_the_cross

pictures.scene: William Holman Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ standing alone at night in a long white robe under a heavy embroidered cloak clasped with jewels, a crown of thorns on His head with a thin gold halo behind it, raising His right hand to knock at a shut door that has no handle and is grown over with weeds, ivy and brambles, and carrying in His left hand a pierced iron lantern whose candle throws a warm red light up the door and out across the dark orchard grass and the windfall apples at His bare feet, with bare branches and a faint blue night sky beyond, walk while you have the light, so that darkness will not overtake you, …
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: Jan de Bray, King David Playing the Harp — a grey bearded king in a long white robe with a gold chain over his shoulder and a blue sash, a small gold crown set on a yellow silk turban, his eyes lifted and his mouth open as he sings, both hands in among the strings of a tall carved red harp held against his knee, and pressed close behind him a laurel crowned singer with his head thrown back, another old face leaning in at the strings, brass horns lifted at the top corner and an open music book held up in the shadow at the right, with a plain grey stone pier and a dark doorway above them, lord, who has believed our message, and to whom has the arm of the lord been revealed, …
pictures.name: pd_de_bray_king_david_playing_the_harp

pictures.scene: John Everett Millais, The Blind Girl — a red haired beggar girl sitting on the grass at the edge of a meadow with her eyes shut and her face lifted to the warmth, a brown cloak drawn over her head and a wide gold brown skirt spread round her, a small concertina resting on her lap and a paper label at her throat, her fair haired little sister leaning in against her shoulder with one hand in hers and the other holding the cloak up to look out from under it, a tortoiseshell butterfly settled on the cloak, and behind them a brilliant green field with cattle, sheep and a white horse, a village of red roofs and a church on the ridge, and a double rainbow standing in the dark storm sky, he has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, …
pictures.name: pd_millais_the_blind_girl

pictures.scene: Fra Angelico, Christ Glorified in the Court of Heaven — Christ seated high in a deep blue almond shaped glory ringed with little blue cherub heads, robed in pale blue and white with a gold rayed halo behind His fair hair, one hand lifted in blessing and the other opened out, a great burst of gold and red rays spreading behind Him and the whole ground of the panel burnished gold scored with ruled lines, ranks of haloed saints and angels standing and kneeling on blue clouds down both sides with their hands pressed together, and below Him a winged angel in a dark blue gown holding up the cross, isaiah said these things because he saw jesus' glory and spoke about him, …
pictures.name: pd_fra_angelico_christ_in_glory

pictures.scene: Vasily Perov, The Refectory — a rich lady sweeping into a vaulted monastery hall in a wide lilac silk crinoline with a white shawl and a bonnet, a decorated old gentleman in a black tailcoat and white trousers on her arm, a bearded monk in a tall black klobuk bowing low in front of her with his hand spread out in welcome, another brother bent almost double at her skirt, a monk lying flat on the stone floor at her feet, more faces crowding in behind, and at the right edge a ragged beggar woman with her hands flung up and her barefoot children sprawled on the flags, whom nobody is looking at, under pale painted vaults hung with dark garlands, for they loved praise from men more than praise from god, …
pictures.name: pd_perov_kloostermaaltijd

pictures.scene: Albrecht Durer, The Vision of the Seven Candlesticks — a woodcut cut all over in close black line, Christ seated in the clouds in a wide robe of heavy folds with a blaze of rays round His head and a long beard falling over His chest, an open book of letters held before Him and a two edged sword coming out of His mouth, His right hand stretched out holding seven burning stars, tall wrought candlesticks with lit candles standing in a ring on either side of Him and rolling banks of cloud filling every corner, and John fallen on his face at the bottom of the picture in a great sweep of drapery with his bare feet thrown out behind him, i have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in me should remain in darkness, …
pictures.name: pd_durer_the_vision_of_the_seven_candlesticks

pictures.scene: Caspar David Friedrich, The Cross in the Mountains — a wooden crucifix standing alone on the top of a rocky summit, turned away from us and seen in dark silhouette against the sky, with a small gilded figure of Christ on it catching the last light, rose coloured crags climbing to it out of the dark, tall black firs rising on either side and in the hollows below, and behind it all a sunset sky banded with heavy violet cloud and burning orange, with three long pale shafts of light striking up from a sun that has already gone down, for i have not come to judge the world, but to save the world, …
pictures.name: pd_friedrich_the_cross_in_the_mountains

lines.text: Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, the hometown of Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
So they hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served, and Lazarus was among those reclining at the table with Him.
Then Mary took about a pint of expensive perfume, made of pure nard, and she anointed Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair. And the house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.
But one of His disciples, Judas Iscariot, who was going to betray Him, asked,
Why wasn't this perfume sold for three hundred denarii and the money given to the poor?
Judas did not say this because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief. As keeper of the money bag, he used to take from what was put into it.
Leave her alone, Jesus replied. She has kept this perfume in preparation for the day of My burial.
The poor you will always have with you, but you will not always have Me.
Meanwhile a large crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there. And they came not only because of Him, but also to see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests made plans to kill Lazarus as well,
for on account of him many of the Jews were deserting them and believing in Jesus.
The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem.
They took palm branches and went out to meet Him, shouting: Hosanna! Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord! Blessed is the King of Israel!
Finding a young donkey, Jesus sat on it, as it is written:
Do not be afraid, O Daughter of Zion. See, your King is coming, seated on the colt of a donkey.

At first His disciples did not understand these things, but after Jesus was glorified they remembered what had been done to Him, and they realized that these very things had also been written about Him.
Meanwhile, many people continued to testify that they had been with Jesus when He called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.
That is also why the crowd went out to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.
Then the Pharisees said to one another, You can see that this is doing you no good. Look how the whole world has gone after Him!
Now there were some Greeks among those who went up to worship at the feast.
They came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and requested of him, Sir, we want to see Jesus.
Philip relayed this appeal to Andrew, and both of them went and told Jesus.
But Jesus replied, The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
Truly, truly, I tell you, unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a seed; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
Whoever loves his life will lose it, but whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone serves Me, he must follow Me; and where I am, My servant will be as well. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save Me from this hour? No, it is for this purpose that I have come to this hour.
Father, glorify Your name! Then a voice came from heaven: I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.
The crowd standing there heard it and said that it had thundered. Others said that an angel had spoken to Him.
In response, Jesus said, This voice was not for My benefit, but yours.
Now judgment is upon this world; now the prince of this world will be cast out.
And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to Myself.
He said this to indicate the kind of death He was going to die.
The crowd replied, We have heard from the Law that the Christ will remain forever. So how can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?

Then Jesus told them, For a little while longer, the Light will be among you. Walk while you have the Light, so that darkness will not overtake you. The one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
While you have the Light, believe in the Light, so that you may become sons of light. After Jesus had spoken these things, He went away and was hidden from them.
Although Jesus had performed so many signs in their presence, they still did not believe in Him.
This was to fulfill the word of Isaiah the prophet: Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?
For this reason they were unable to believe. For again, Isaiah says:
He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they cannot see with their eyes, and understand with their hearts, and turn, and I would heal them.
Isaiah said these things because he saw Jesus' glory and spoke about Him.
Nevertheless, many of the leaders believed in Him; but because of the Pharisees they did not confess Him, for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue.
For they loved praise from men more than praise from God.
Then Jesus cried out, Whoever believes in Me does not believe in Me alone, but in the One who sent Me.
And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.
I have come into the world as a light, so that no one who believes in Me should remain in darkness.
As for anyone who hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him. For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
There is a judge for the one who rejects Me and does not receive My words: The word that I have spoken will judge him on the last day.
I have not spoken on My own, but the Father who sent Me has commanded Me what to say and how to say it.
And I know that His command leads to eternal life. So I speak exactly what the Father has told Me to say.
